$comment: ARM what-if NOISE allowlist — consumed by scripts/ci/whatif-drift-verdict.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Microsoft documents the false-positive class directly:
'Some of the properties that are listed as deleted won't actually change.
Properties can be incorrectly reported as deleted when they aren't in the
Bicep file, but are automatically set during deployment as default values.
This result is considered "noise" in the what-if response.'
— https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-resource-manager/bicep/deploy-what-if
RULES OF THE ALLOWLIST (enforced by the script, not by convention):
1. Only propertyChangeType Delete / NoEffect is ever suppressible. A
Create or Modify on a property is a genuine template-vs-live conflict
and is NEVER suppressed.
2. A resource drops out of the drift verdict only when EVERY one of its
property deltas is allowlisted. One unmatched delta keeps the whole
resource as real drift.
3. Every suppressed delta is still printed (step summary + artifact
suppressed-list.txt) so suppression is auditable, never silent.
4. Adding an entry requires a `reason` grounded in the resource's ARM
schema (read-only / server-defaulted / service-managed). Do not add a
property you merely find inconvenient — encode it in bicep instead.
5. A `path` may carry `*` in place of an ARM array index. `*` matches ONLY
digits, in either shape what-if emits (`.0` or `[0]`) — never a property
name — so it cannot blanket a subtree. Add the element form only when a
real what-if run has actually emitted it.
6. VALUE PREDICATE. If the `reason` justifies suppression with the value
the property was MEASURED to hold — 'Measured before=0', 'Server-
defaulted to False' — the rule MUST carry `whenBeforeEquals` (one
literal, compared structurally and without coercion) or `whenBeforeIn`
(a list of them). Without it the rule matches on PATH ONLY and
suppresses that property at every value, including the value the reason
says it can never hold: the APIM legacy-protocol toggles are allowlisted
precisely BECAUSE ARM defaults them to the secure 'False', and a
path-only rule hid a live 'True' — SSL 3.0 actually ENABLED — just as
quietly. That is a detection regression and a deploy-integrity R7
violation (the reason asserts a condition the code never established).
The whatif-drift-verdict self-test enforces this: a reason that cites a
measured value with no predicate FAILS the suite. Read-only ARM metadata
with no fixed value (privateDnsZoneConfigs id/etag/type, RP-assigned
endpoints) legitimately carries no predicate — its reason cites no value.
A predicate that does not match live is the SAFE direction: the delta
stays in the drift verdict, visible, instead of being hidden.
Seeded 2026-07-28 from run 30259654971 (issue #2540): 11/11 Modify deltas
were this class — 9 identical UAMI deltas plus Grafana + the UDF Container
App. See docs/fiab/runbooks/bicep-drift.md.
Extended 2026-09-07 from run 33406666389 (issue #3191). That run's 128 real
resources carried 357 unmatched property deltas; a per-property census of the
raw what-if document (not the 6-per-resource truncated list) showed the
largest families were all server-defaulted or read-only, each confirmed
against its recorded `before` value. The entries added below cover 138 of
those 357 deltas. The rest — AAS asAdministrators, APIM policy bodies,
diagnosticSettings whole log categories, ACR networkRuleSet, KV createMode,
the managedEnvironments block — are REAL template-vs-live conflicts and are
deliberately left in the verdict for a reconciling bicep change.
Hardened 2026-09-07 (PR #4343 review). Those entries were added with the
measured `before` value written into the reason but never checked by the
matcher, which matched on PATH ALONE. Measured inversion: a synthetic APIM
Delete on Gateway.Security.Protocols.Ssl30 carrying before='True' — SSL 3.0
actually ENABLED in live — was suppressed to '0 real delta(s), 1 what-if
noise suppressed', exit 0, drift list empty. Same for retentionPolicy.days
with before=365. Rule 6 (the value predicate) closes that: 19 of the 35
rules now pin the value their reason cites, and the self-test fails any
reason that cites a measured value without one.

Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedId.reason: identity.bicep declares no `properties` block (a UAMI has none to set). The RP populates isolationScope='None' (the default of the None|Regional enum, 2024-11-30 schema) plus the read-only clientId/principalId/tenantId. what-if therefore reports the whole `properties` object as Delete on EVERY UAMI in the estate. The subset guard means a future settable property (e.g. assignmentRestrictions) would NOT be suppressed.

Same as above when what-if reports the leaf rather than the parent object. Server-defaulted to 'None' (the default of the None|Regional enum); a redeploy that omits it is a no-op. The predicate means a UAMI whose live isolationScope is 'Regional' — a value the template does not declare and a redeploy WOULD reset — stays real drift.

Microsoft.Dashboard/grafana.reason: Service-managed lifecycle. Azure Managed Grafana upgrades the major version in place; admin-plane/main.bicep deliberately does not pin it (pinning would make a from-scratch deploy fail in any cloud/region where that major is not yet offered — Gov lags Commercial). The template expressing no opinion is the intent, not drift. If Loom ever needs a pinned version, set it in bicep and DELETE this entry.
Read-only — the RP-assigned Grafana URL (surfaced as the grafanaEndpoint output).
Read-only — the exact running Grafana build, chosen by the service.

Microsoft.App/containerApps.reason: Read-only runtime state ('Running'), never settable in a template.

Server-defaulted to 'Consumption' on a Consumption-only managed environment; udf-runtime.bicep omits it deliberately so the same template works on Consumption and workload-profile environments. The predicate matters because the property IS settable: an app live on a dedicated profile ('D4', 'E8') that the template omits WOULD be moved back to Consumption by a redeploy, so that shape stays real drift.

Server-defaulted to 100. Omitted by template; a redeploy re-applies the same default. Settable, so the predicate keeps a live non-default (an app deliberately pinned to 5) in the verdict rather than hiding the reset a redeploy would perform.

Server-defaulted to [{latestRevision:true, weight:100}] under activeRevisionsMode 'Single'. Declaring it would fight the roll workflows that shift traffic — which is exactly why the predicate is pinned to the all-on-latest shape: a live traffic SPLIT (a stuck blue/green weight distribution the template does not describe) is a real estate state and stays in the verdict.
Server-defaulted to 0 for non-TCP transports. A live non-zero exposedPort is a TCP ingress the template does not declare, so it stays real drift.

Microsoft.Network/privateDnsZones/virtua.reason: Server-defaulted. `resolutionPolicy` was added in the 2024-06-01 privateDnsZones schema as a Default|NxDomainRedirect enum; the RP stamps 'Default' on every link, including the ~27 links private-dns.bicep creates without expressing an opinion. Measured before='Default' on every occurrence in run 33406666389 — a redeploy that omits it re-applies the same value. The predicate holds the suppression to that measurement: a link live on 'NxDomainRedirect' would be RESET by a redeploy, so it stays real drift. If Loom ever needs NxDomainRedirect, set it in bicep and DELETE this entry.

Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints.reason: Server-defaulted to false. A dual-stack flag the RP stamps on every private endpoint under the newer network API versions; private-endpoint.bicep declares only IPv4 subnets, so what-if reports the RP's own false as a deletion. Measured before=false on every occurrence in run 33406666389. The predicate is what keeps this from hiding the inverse: an endpoint live with IPv6 ENABLED that the template does not declare would be turned off by a redeploy, and that stays real drift.

Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/priva.reason: Read-only — the ARM resource ID the RP assigns to each generated privateDnsZoneConfigs child. The template declares each config by name + privateDnsZoneId only; the full child ID is never settable.
Read-only — RP-assigned concurrency tag on each generated config.
Read-only — the ARM type discriminator ('Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/privateDnsZoneGroups/privateDnsZoneConfigs') the RP stamps on each generated config.
Read-only lifecycle state ('Succeeded'), never settable in a template.

Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings.reason: Server-defaulted remnant of a RETIRED feature. Diagnostic-setting-level retention was retired in favour of Log Analytics workspace / storage lifecycle retention; the RP still materializes `retentionPolicy:{enabled:false,days:0}` on every category. Measured before=0 on every occurrence in run 33406666389, so a redeploy that omits it re-applies the same zero. The predicate is load-bearing: on a category that still carries a real retention (before=365, a legacy setting from before the retirement) a redeploy WOULD drop it to 0, so that shape stays real drift. NOTE: this suppresses ONLY the retention leaf — a Delete of a whole `properties.logs.N` category (the template declaring fewer categories than live) stays real drift and keeps the resource in the verdict.

Server-defaulted remnant of the same retired retention feature, on the metrics side: the RP materializes `retentionPolicy:{enabled:false,days:0}` on every metric category. Measured before=0 on every occurrence in run 33406666389; same predicate, same reason, so a non-zero live retention stays visible.

Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sq.reason: Cosmos DB's documented default indexing policy. A container created without an explicit indexingPolicy is stamped with includedPaths=[{path:'/*'}] — measured verbatim as the before value in run 33406666389, and pinned here as the predicate. Because only a Delete is ever suppressible (rule 1), this can only fire when the template declares no indexing policy for that container; the predicate adds the second half — live must ALSO still be the server default. A container someone hand-tuned to index a narrower path set stays real drift, because a redeploy would widen it back to '/*'.

The other half of Cosmos DB's default indexing policy: excludedPaths=[{path:'/"_etag"/?'}], the system-managed _etag exclusion. Measured verbatim as the before value in run 33406666389 and pinned as the predicate — a live exclusion list with anything MORE than the _etag entry is a hand-tuned policy a redeploy would discard, so it stays real drift.

Same default _etag exclusion, for the containers where what-if reported the array ELEMENT rather than the whole array. Both granularities occur in run 33406666389 and which one ARM emits is not stable; the predicate is the same measured shape, one element deep.

Read-only projection of the ACCOUNT-level backup policy onto the container. backupPolicy is settable on Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts, not on a container; the RP echoes the account's policy ({type:1} = Continuous, measured in run 33406666389) into every container's resource body. cosmos.bicep sets it once on the account, which is the correct place. The predicate pins the Continuous shape: if the account's policy is ever something else, the echo changes with it and the delta surfaces rather than being silently absorbed here.

Server-defaulted. Under the default LastWriterWins conflict-resolution mode Cosmos stamps conflictResolutionPath='/_ts' — measured verbatim in run 33406666389. The templates declare no conflict-resolution policy, so the RP default is re-applied on redeploy. A container whose live path is a custom property (a deliberate LWW tiebreaker) would be reset to /_ts by that redeploy, so the predicate keeps it in the verdict.

Microsoft.ApiManagement/service.reason: Server-defaulted, and defaulted to the SECURE value. APIM stamps the legacy-protocol toggles as 'False' (disabled) when the template does not mention them — measured before='False' in run 33406666389 — so omitting it neither enables SSL 3.0 nor changes anything on redeploy. THE PREDICATE IS THE WHOLE POINT: the justification is the VALUE, not the path, so the rule only applies at that value. A live 'True' means SSL 3.0 is actually ENABLED on the gateway, which is real drift the lane must show — and a path-only rule would have suppressed exactly that. Suppressing the secure case does NOT drop the APIM service from the verdict: that resource also carries Modify deltas (developerPortalStatus, legacyPortalStatus, natGatewayState) which rule 1 never suppresses.

Same legacy-protocol toggle on the backend (gateway-to-backend) side. Measured before='False' — the secure default — in run 33406666389, and the predicate holds the suppression to that value: a live 'True' is SSL 3.0 enabled toward backends and stays real drift.
Same legacy-protocol toggle on the backend side. Measured before='False' — the secure default — in run 33406666389; a live 'True' is TLS 1.0 actually enabled and is never suppressed.
Same legacy-protocol toggle on the backend side. Measured before='False' — the secure default — in run 33406666389; a live 'True' is TLS 1.1 actually enabled and is never suppressed.
